lines.text: BirunIQ.
Sovereign spatial intelligence.
This is BirunIQ. One platform for geospatial intelligence. One map, one catalog of layers, one sign-in. So an agency, or many departments, can work from the same picture.

It's built in Rust, on Postgres and PostGIS, with a React web client, a Flutter field app, and model inference in a containerised sidecar. It deploys three ways: as SaaS, as a sovereign hybrid, or as an air-gap capable build for customers who need a lockout.
Seventeen industries, live today. From defence and critical infrastructure, to environment, agriculture, and land.
A hundred and thirty-three modules. A hundred and thirty department modules, and three platform modules. Plus thirty shared capabilities in the registry.

One deployment can serve many tenants. Each tenant is licensed for the editions it needs. Its data is kept apart by row-level security in the database. And inside a tenant, access is scoped by team. So it's one system, for many departments.
Start with defence and security. WatchFloor is the command picture. Protected assets on one map, each with its own record.
MaritimeLens flags radar detections with no matching ship signal. Dark vessels. And it says so when it can't tell.
Sentry watches named sites. Each gets a risk score, and the drivers behind it, and incidents land in a console.
Guardian scores the infrastructure itself. Starting with energy.
Then bridges and tunnels. Four products, one system underneath.
Now critical infrastructure. In this view, every asset stands at its stored risk score. Taller means more severe.
Grid command. Outages, transformer records, transmission lines.
Then network operations, where assets cluster by count, and open into icons as you zoom.
Flux. Storage state of charge, generation against its rating, corridors against their limits.
PetroCore watches a site for change, camera by camera. All of it simulated. The screen says so.
Dark contacts at loading points. And process-safety impairments, plant by plant.
Milepost keeps bridge inspections. Tower keeps airport lighting. Different industries. The same platform.
Environmental. SpillTrace records an incident, the slick area seen on each pass, and the receptors in its path.
FloodSurge sets critical facilities against FEMA flood zones. Then modelled streamflow, and river gauges.
GreenScope. Findings with inspection photos, and risk by zone.
Groundwater. Over thirteen hundred monitoring wells, clustered by count. Zoom in, and they open into well records.
Even over satellite imagery.
And Harvest. A crop calendar, a crop index from satellite imagery, and field boundaries the model delineated. Real model output, not demo.
Government and land. Atlas is the smart-city view. Sensors with a 24 hour trend, assets, incidents, emergency units.
Maritime shows vessels with their stored tracks. And a mapbook can be generated straight from the current view.
Terra turns drone imagery into candidate parcels, reviewed one at a time. They're proposals. Not titles.
One Africa runs a port. Vessels, terminals, berth occupancy.
And Blueprint tracks construction projects.
Underneath all of it is one platform. Layers come from one catalog. Analysis and compare work the same way everywhere. Here, satellite imagery against streets.
And this is the Admin console. Which editions a tenant is licensed for. Which modules are switched on. Field apps, and data sources. And one control for external data. All from the same sign-in.
Every external feed is listed, with its status. And a tenant can switch external data off.
BirunIQ Field brings captures from the mobile app back into the same system.
Defence. Energy. Environment. Land. One system.
Unlock the evidence.
Unlock the answers.
Unlock your world.
